title: He was chosen…
paragraphs:
He was chosen…
but still thrown away.
Because somewhere deep inside, you thought God’s favor would protect you from being hurt like that.
And maybe… your life does too.

You were faithful.
You stayed pure.
You obeyed when it was hard.

Still misunderstood.
Still overlooked.
Still treated like your calling meant nothing.
So now you’re asking the quiet question no one hears:
“If God is with me… why did this happen?”
Because this is where most people break.
But in the confusion inside the pit.
Joseph didn’t just lose comfort—he lost trust.

His own brothers.
His own blood.
The ones who should’ve protected him…

Genesis tells us they stripped him of his robe—the very symbol of favor (Genesis 37:23).
Read that again.

The thing that marked him as chosen
was the thing that made him a target.

Favor doesn’t repel betrayal.
It often exposes the hearts around you.
And that’s the part we don’t preach.

We celebrate the palace.
We quote the promise.
But we skip the pit.

It’s where your theology gets tested.
It’s where your identity gets questioned.
It’s where your faith either deepens… or dies.

Have you ever smiled in public…
but wrestled with silent disappointment in God?

Have you ever obeyed God outwardly…
but inwardly started negotiating with compromise?

Delayed obedience.
Quiet bitterness.
Subtle pride that whispers, “I deserved better.”
We don’t say it out loud.

Sometimes the greatest danger isn’t what people did to you…
it’s what betrayal is slowly turning you into.
Joseph had every reason to become bitter.

He could’ve hardened.
He could’ve justified revenge.
He could’ve rewritten his story as a victim.
Because even in the pit, he understood something deeper:
God’s presence did not leave him.

Scripture says, “The Lord was with Joseph” (Genesis 39:2)—
not in the palace…
Some scholars interpret this as a theological anchor—that God’s favor is not measured by external success, but by His unbroken presence.
Because if God is still with you in the betrayal…
then the betrayal is not your end.
Joseph’s story is not just about survival.
He wasn’t just sold for silver—He was handed over by the very people He came to save (Matthew 26:14–16).
Isaiah says, “He was pierced for our transgressions… crushed for our iniquities” (Isaiah 53:5).
Here’s the truth we don’t like:

Your deepest problem is not what they did to you.
It’s the sin inside you that needs saving.
Jesus didn’t just endure betrayal—He absorbed the punishment your sin deserved.

On that cross, He carried your bitterness.
Your pride.
Your hidden compromises.
Your silent rebellion.
That means forgiveness is not earned—it’s received.
But it requires something most people avoid:
Letting God deal not just with what hurt you…
…but with what’s growing inside you because of it.

Some people want healing without surrender—
but God will not heal what you insist on hiding.

Not polished.
Not explained away.
Not justified.

Let Him heal what people broke.
Let Him cleanse what sin corrupted.
Let Him restore what pride distorted.

You are not abandoned.
You are not forgotten.
You are not defined by what they did.

You are not the betrayed version of yourself.
You are the redeemed child God is forming through the fire.
God is already turning for good (Genesis 50:20).
You may not see it yet.
But heaven is not confused about your story.
Let it lead you to surrender—not shame.
And if this stirred something in you…
Because next… we’re going to talk about what Joseph did in the prison that most believers still ignore.
And it might expose more than you expect.
